subject: Renewal uplift structuring — tranche billing & short-term SLA adjustment
messages:
From: Sara Lim <sara@hearthhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@hearthhealth.com
Date: 2026-10-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal + mid-contract expansion question

Sean —

Thanks for taking a quick look. We ran the Q3 usage numbers and expect an uplift: approximately a 45% increase in token consumption for the next 6 months as we enable a new feature across our clinical workflows (attached: HearthHealth_Usage_Q3.csv). Budget is tight this quarter — procurement asked whether Redwood can support: 1) staged billing (split uplift across two invoices), and 2) a temporary concession on SLA (we can tolerate slightly higher latency during the rollout window) in exchange for a lower uplift rate.

Can you confirm if those two levers are feasible and what the timeline looks like to get an amendment in place? We should target sign-off by early November.

—Sara
Sara Lim
Head of Platform @ HearthHealth

Attachments: HearthHealth_Usage_Q3.csv
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara@hearthhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + mid-contract expansion question

Hi Sara — thanks for the context and the usage file. High level — we can typically support both staged billing and a temporary SLA adjustment, but we'll need to formalize the tradeoffs so procurement has a clear comparison. Two quick options we can propose:

- Option A (staggered uplift): 50% of the additional reserved units/invoice now, 50% billed next quarter; standard SLA retained; small admin fee for mid-cycle amendment.
- Option B (blended concession + SLA window): Offer a blended uplift rate (lowered by ~10–15%) if HearthHealth accepts a 90-day temporary SLA waiver (higher latency SLO for the rollout). We would automatically revert to standard SLA after the window.

I’m looping in Kimberly for pricing play and Marcus for the invoicing cadence/contract language. 

Kimberly/Marcus — can you review and propose a concrete blended rate and an invoice schedule we can present? Sara — can you confirm the expected additional reserved units or monthly token estimate so we can run the numbers?

I’ll draft an amendment skeleton (no legalese) once we agree on the scenario.

Thanks,
Sean
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Sara Lim <sara@hearthhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + mid-contract expansion question

Sara — appreciate the usage detail. Based on the 45% uplift indicated and our uplift bands, here are two priced scenarios (ballpark, subject to final numbers):

1) Staggered billing (no SLA change)
   - Incremental reserved units: equivalent to ~420M tokens/month
   - Invoice schedule: 50% charged 10/31, remaining 50% charged 1/31
   - Rate: current renewal rate + 18% uplift (no blending)
   - Pros: preserves SLA, minimal legal work (amendment + invoice schedule)

2) Blended concession (with temporary SLA window)
   - Incremental reserved units: same
   - Invoice schedule: single amendment; uplift blended across current term and uplift tranche
   - Rate: current renewal rate + 12% blended uplift if HearthHealth accepts a 90-day SLA adjustment (we'd move from 99.9% to 99.5% availability for that period; detailed SLO table in SLA_change_request.docx)
   - Pros: lower unit economics for HearthHealth; Redwood accepts measured, temporary risk during rollout

Operational notes: for Option 2 we need a signed PO + explicit acknowledgement of the temporary SLA change in the amendment. Marcus — on invoicing, if Procurement needs Net30 vs Net45 we can accommodate with slight fee offset.

Sara — if you can confirm the PO timing and whether procurement requires split invoices (vs single invoice with payment plan), I’ll convert these into a short amendment draft and provide the DocuSign link.

-Kimberly
Director, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: SLA_change_request.docx
From: Sara Lim <sara@hearthhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@hearthhealth.com
Date: 2026-10-13T19:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + mid-contract expansion question

Thanks Kimberly — this is helpful. Procurement confirms the following:

- They prefer Option 2 (blended concession with SLA window) provided the blended uplift is <= 13% and the SLA change is limited to 90 days and explicitly reversible.
- PO target: they can issue PO by 2026-10-28 if amendment and DocuSign link are delivered by 2026-10-20.
- Payment terms: Net30. If we can split invoicing (two invoices) that would be easier for internal approvals, but they can accept a single invoice with staged payment schedule.

We are good to move forward — can you send the amendment draft and DocuSign for internal review? I attached a short procurement checklist for your reference.

—Sara

Attachments: HearthHealth_procurement_checklist.pdf
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara@hearthhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + mid-contract expansion question

Sara/Kimberly/Marcus — quick confirmation after internal review:

- Final commercial: blended uplift capped at 12% (meets HearthHealth ask of <=13%).
- SLA concession: 90-day window, SLO drops to 99.5% availability for the window; auto-revert clause included.
- Invoice approach: Redwood will issue two invoices per Kimberly's Option B recommendation (50/50) over the next two billing cycles; terms Net30.
- Deliverables by 2026-10-20: amendment draft + DocuSign envelope. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/envelope/EXAMPLE-ENVELOPE-12345

Marcus — please prepare the amendment (HearthHealth_Amendment_draft_v2.pdf) and the HubSpot deal note (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/7421). Sara — once you confirm PO timing I’ll send the envelope for signature.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we’ll aim to have the signed amendment and PO in place before your 10/28 procurement deadline.

Best,
Sean
